v.why: Raising an already large Adam step size causes divergence and collapse to majority-class accuracy, as in probes 13-16.
At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so a larger step gives large gains (probes 9-12).
Large batches mean fewer updates per epoch, so increasing the step size compensates more strongly (probes 5, 11).
With a small learning rate, fewer updates from a larger batch leave the model further undertrained (probes 21-23, 33).
At low learning rates, extra layers add capacity and faster effective fitting without instability (probes 61, 62, 65, 66, 69, 70).
Deeper ReLU nets are more prone to instability and dead units at high step sizes (probes 64, 72, 78).
When L2 is already strong, increasing it further over-regularizes toward underfitting on every dataset (probes 89-92), while it is negligible at small alpha.
Adding units matters most when the network is narrow and capacity-limited, with diminishing returns at large widths.
Widening deeper nets improves trainability and gradient flow; probes 50, 52, 56, 58, 60 are positive versus mixed or negative at depth 1.
Going up from very small batches reduces gradient noise at little cost in update count, whereas at large batches it mainly cuts updates and hurts.

raw:
Here are ten interaction hypotheses. Each is grounded in the 100 single-seed probes and in how Adam-trained ReLU MLPs usually behave. Because the probes are single-seed, swings of about 1–2 points are within noise. I put more weight on the larger, consistent patterns:

- **Learning rate:** raising it is catastrophic when it is already high (probes 13–16). It helps most when it is low and the batch is large, where updates are few and small (probes 5 and 11).
- **Batch size:** raising it hurts at low learning rates, because it cuts the number of updates (probes 21–23, 33).
- **Depth:** adding layers helps at low learning rates (probes 61, 62, 65, 66, 69, 70). It is destructive at high learning rates (probes 64, 72, 78).
- **Alpha:** raising it when it is already strong collapses accuracy on every dataset (probes 89–92).
- **Width:** adding units helps more for deeper networks (probes 50, 52, 56, 58, 60 versus 49, 55, 59).
